_doc: Body-shop-manager automation tuning (#316, parent #297). The decision-function knobs the on-staff body-shop manager uses once its `shop_throughput` clears each function's gate in tunables.json#managerGates.bodyShopManager.actThresholds. The Tier-3 mirror of data/service-manager.json. The Body Shop has ONE pricing/marketing lever — the insurance↔retail `channel` posture (the locked satellite table's 'channel choice') — so this file has a `channel` block where Service has separate `posture` + `marketing` blocks; there are no separate mailer arms to tune. All magnitudes are placeholders pending the S14 calibration pass (#286).

par._doc: Demand-driven par tuning over the four collision categories. The manager sets each category's target/reorderPoint off its trailing intake demand (the BodyShopInsights demand-heat window count). target = max(minTarget, ceil(demand x targetCoverDays)); reorderPoint = max(minReorderPoint, ceil(demand x reorderCoverDays)), capped at target. Identical shape to the serviceManager par engine.

channel._doc: Reputation-driven insurance↔retail channel posture [0,1] (0 = full insurance-DRP lean, 1 = full retail customer-pay). This single lever is the Body Shop's unified pricing AND marketing decision: leaning retail both raises the player-priced markup and skews CollisionStream's demand mix toward fatter customer-pay jobs. A strong reputation lets the manager lean into retail (win + price up customer-pay work without losing it); a weak one stays on rate-capped insurance volume to keep the bays fed. posture = lerp(minPosture, maxPosture, clamp01((reputation - floor)/(ceil - floor))).

capacity._doc: Capacity-aware rush balancing. Once the capacity function is automated the manager makes the rush-vs-walk call capacity-aware — it only rush-orders a parts miss while the shop has slack (live utilization below the ceiling), otherwise it walks the job rather than overcommit a slammed bay/advisor floor.
